今天的主题：职场沟通和工作压力。这组词对 G 类特别实用：写作 Task 1 的投诉信、给同事或经理的信，阅读 Section 2 的员工手册和公司规定，口语 Part 1 的 Work 话题，以及 Task 2 讨论「工作压力」「职场关系」时都用得上。

例句

  • Please keep your tone polite, even if the customer is hostile.（就算顾客有敌意，也请保持礼貌的语气。）
  • My colleague took all the credit for the project, which really annoyed me.（我同事把项目的功劳全揽走了，这让我很恼火。）
  • I feel anxious when my workload is heavy and the deadline is close.（工作量大、截止日期又近的时候，我会很焦虑。）
  • She decided to resign because she couldn't accomplish anything in that team.（她决定辞职，因为她在那个团队里什么也做不成。）
  • All personnel must report safety problems to a senior manager.（所有员工都必须把安全问题报告给高级经理。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 colleague、workload、deadline 写一句你自己的工作情况，G 类写信和口语 Part 1 都能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Rude emails（粗鲁的邮件）。这集讲职场邮件里哪些做法让人觉得没礼貌：开头只写名字不打招呼、精心写的长邮件只回一个表情、抄送领导给人施压、不回或者只回一半。心理学家 Emma Russell 用「战斗或逃跑」反应解释为什么人一忙一累就容易写出粗鲁的邮件。这集比较短，句子不难，而且讲的正是 G 类写信最要注意的「语气」，适合精听加积累。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：去年要求美国政府员工列出一周完成的五件事、否则辞职的邮件是谁发的？a) Donald Trump b) JD Vance c) Elon Musk。顺便听出：听众举了哪两个粗鲁邮件的例子？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Claudia Hammond、Peter Olusoga 和 Emma Russell 三段是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍，尤其是 Emma Russell 讲 fight response 和 flight response 那段。
  4. 第三遍挑 Phil 讲老板抢功劳那段（"The fight response can make us belittle someone..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：put someone on the defensive（让人产生戒备）、uncivil（无礼的）、belittle（贬低）、put someone in their place（让人认清自己的位置）、get something off your plate（把事情甩出去）、frazzled（疲惫焦躁的）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Phil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Phil.

Phil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是菲尔。

Becca：And I'm Becca.

Becca：我是贝卡。

Phil：Sending emails is a big part of modern work, and most people try to write emails politely礼貌的. Most, but not all! Recently, BBC Radio 4 programme All in the Mind asked listeners to tell them what they find rude in emails. Here, presenter Claudia Hammond and guest Pete Olusoga discuss what listeners had to say:

Phil：发邮件是现代工作的一大部分，大多数人写邮件都尽量礼貌。是大多数，但不是所有人！最近，BBC 第四电台的节目《心灵之中》请听众说说他们觉得邮件里哪些东西很粗鲁。下面是主持人克劳迪娅·哈蒙德和嘉宾皮特·奥卢索加在讨论听众的来信：

Claudia Hammond：Rachel in Manchester says what annoys使恼火 her is people who start their emails with just your name and without a simple greeting问候语 like 'hi'. She says the unnecessary formality拘泥形式 always has the effect of putting her immediately on the defensive.

Claudia Hammond：曼彻斯特的蕾切尔说，让她恼火的是那些邮件开头只写你的名字、连一句简单的「你好」都没有的人。她说这种没必要的生硬正式，总是让她马上产生戒备心理。

Dr Peter Olusoga：We've got an anonymous匿名的 one here, who recently received a single emoji表情符号 in response to a carefully considered and worded精心思考、斟酌措辞的 email.

Dr Peter Olusoga：这里有一位匿名听众，他最近精心思考、斟酌措辞写了一封邮件，结果对方只回了一个表情符号。

Becca：One listener doesn't like emails which start with just her name because they put her on the defensive让她产生戒备. The phrase to put someone on the defensive让人产生戒备 means to do or say something which makes them feel threatened威胁，使感到受威胁 or unsure.

Becca：有一位听众不喜欢开头只写她名字的邮件，因为这让她产生戒备。短语 put someone on the defensive 的意思是，做某事或说某话让对方感到受威胁或者没把握。

Phil：Another listener found it rude when their email was answered with a single emoji表情符号, and I think that would annoy使恼火 me too. These emails are examples of people being uncivil无礼的 – an adjective meaning rude or impolite. And just to note, the noun that goes with this is incivility无礼行为. In this episode, we'll be hearing more about rude emails at work and, as usual, we'll be learning some useful new vocabulary, all of which you can find on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Phil：另一位听众觉得自己的邮件只得到一个表情符号的回复很不礼貌，我想我也会被惹恼。这些邮件都是人们 uncivil 的例子，这个形容词的意思是粗鲁、没礼貌。顺便说一下，对应的名词是 incivility。这一期我们会听到更多关于职场粗鲁邮件的内容，和往常一样，我们还会学一些有用的新词，所有词汇都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 找到。

Becca：But first, I have a question for you, Phil. Last year, thousands of US government workers received an email requiring them to justify证明……合理 their job by listing five things they had accomplished完成 that week… or resign辞职. But who sent this email? Was it:
a) Donald Trump,
b) JD Vance, or
c) Elon Musk?

Becca：不过先问你一个问题，菲尔。去年，成千上万的美国政府工作人员收到一封邮件，要求他们列出当周完成的五件事来证明自己这份工作有存在的必要，否则就辞职。那么这封邮件是谁发的？是：a）唐纳德·特朗普，b）JD·万斯，还是 c）埃隆·马斯克？

Phil：Ooh, I don't know... Maybe JD Vance?

Phil：哦，我不知道……也许是 JD·万斯？

Becca：We'll find out later in the programme. Now, according to some psychologists心理学家, rudeness in emails is based on a fight-or-flight response战斗或逃跑反应 humans feel when stressed. Here, psychologist心理学家 Dr Emma Russell explains these responses for BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.

Becca：节目后面会揭晓答案。好，按照一些心理学家的说法，邮件里的粗鲁源于人在压力下产生的「战斗或逃跑」反应。下面，心理学家艾玛·拉塞尔博士在 BBC 第四电台的《心灵之中》里解释这些反应。

Dr Emma Russell：So, a fight response战斗反应 is usually when we try to dominate压制，支配 or belittle贬低 other people. Emails that are hostile有敌意的 in tone and language, or even cc'ing抄送 senior高层的 personnel人员，员工 in on the message in order to elevate把问题往上报 an issue and put someone in their place让人认清自己的位置. Then the flight response逃跑反应 is when people try to protect themselves by withdrawing退缩 or avoiding. They won't reply, or if they do reply, maybe they don't answer all of the points in the email. They're just trying to get it off their plate.

Dr Emma Russell：所谓战斗反应，通常是我们想压制或贬低别人。比如邮件的语气和措辞带着敌意，甚至把高层人员抄送进来，为的是把问题往上捅、让某人认清自己的位置。而逃跑反应是人们通过退缩或回避来保护自己。他们不回复，或者就算回复了，也可能不回应邮件里的所有要点。他们只是想把这件事从自己手上甩掉。

Phil：The fight response战斗反应 can make us belittle贬低 someone – make them feel inferior低人一等的 or unimportant. For example, a boss sends a group email in which they give someone else the credit功劳 for the work you did. The boss wants to put you in your place让你认清自己的位置 – an idiom meaning to show someone that they are less important than they think they are.

Phil：战斗反应会让我们去贬低别人，也就是让对方觉得低人一等或者不重要。比如，老板发了一封群发邮件，把你做的工作的功劳算到了别人头上。老板想 put you in your place，这个习语的意思是让某人明白，他们没有自己以为的那么重要。

Becca：The flight response逃跑反应, meanwhile, can be seen when co-workers同事 ignore your message or give a quick, unhelpful reply. Such colleagues want to get work off their plate – another idiom, meaning to remove tasks from your own workload工作量 and give them to someone else to deal with.

Becca：与此同时，逃跑反应体现在同事无视你的消息，或者随便回一句没用的话。这样的同事想 get work off their plate，这是另一个习语，意思是把任务从自己的工作量里移走，交给别人去处理。

Phil：Unfortunately, when stressed and working to a deadline赶截止日期 it's hard to make sure all your emails are polite礼貌的. That's what Emma Russell said when she spoke to BBC Radio 4's All in the Mind.

Phil：遗憾的是，当压力大、又要赶截止日期的时候，很难保证每封邮件都礼貌。艾玛·拉塞尔在 BBC 第四电台的《心灵之中》里就是这么说的。

Dr Emma Russell：Because we're operating in these environments where we are all quite frazzled疲惫焦躁的, we are more at risk of有……的风险 engaging in做出，参与 incivility无礼行为.

Dr Emma Russell：因为我们工作的环境让大家都挺疲惫焦躁的，所以我们更容易做出不礼貌的行为。

Becca：We're more likely to be uncivil无礼的 when we're frazzled疲惫焦躁的 – an informal adjective describing feeling tired or anxious焦虑的 because you're doing too many things at the same time.

Becca：我们 frazzled 的时候更容易失礼。这是个非正式的形容词，形容因为同时做太多事而感到疲惫或焦虑。

Phil：Luckily, there are ways to help. If you feel angry when writing an email, pause before you hit send点发送. One day it might save your friendship or even your job! OK. Becca, I'm going to politely礼貌的 ask you to please reveal the answer to your question.

Phil：好在有办法补救。如果你写邮件时感到生气，点「发送」之前先停一停。说不定哪天这能保住你的友谊，甚至你的工作！好了，贝卡，我要礼貌地请你揭晓你那个问题的答案。

Becca：Of course, Phil. I asked you who sent the email requiring workers to justify证明……合理 their employment or resign辞职.

Becca：当然，菲尔。我问你，是谁发了那封要求员工证明自己工作有必要、否则就辞职的邮件。

Phil：I said that I thought it might have been JD Vance.

Phil：我说我觉得可能是 JD·万斯。

Becca：Well, we're not going to fire you, Phil, but you are wrong. The correct answer was Elon Musk. OK. Let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learnt, starting with the idiom put someone on the defensive让人产生戒备, meaning to make someone feel threatened威胁，使感到受威胁 or unsure.

Becca：嗯，我们不会开除你，菲尔，但你答错了。正确答案是埃隆·马斯克。好，我们来回顾一下学过的词汇，先从习语 put someone on the defensive 开始，意思是让某人感到受威胁或没把握。

Phil：The adjective uncivil无礼的 means impolite, and we have a similar noun that's incivility无礼行为.

Phil：形容词 uncivil 的意思是没礼貌，相关的名词是 incivility。

Becca：To belittle贬低 someone means to make them feel inferior低人一等的 or unimportant.

Becca：belittle someone 的意思是让某人觉得低人一等或不重要。

Phil：If you put someone in their place让人认清自己的位置, you show them that they're not as important as they think they are.

Phil：如果你 put someone in their place，就是让对方明白他们没有自己以为的那么重要。

Becca：To get something off your plate means to give someone else a task or problem instead of dealing with it yourself.

Becca：get something off your plate 的意思是把一项任务或问题交给别人，而不是自己处理。

Phil：And finally, if you're frazzled疲惫焦躁的, you feel tired or anxious焦虑的 because you're doing too much. Once again, our six minutes are up.

Phil：最后，如果你 frazzled，就是因为做的事太多而感到疲惫或焦虑。我们的六分钟又到了。

Becca：If you want to know more about communication at work, check out our series Office English.

Becca：如果你想多了解职场沟通，可以看看我们的系列节目《办公室英语》。

Phil：It's on our website, along with a quiz and a worksheet练习题 for this episode, and that's bbclearningenglish.com. But now it's goodbye.

Phil：它在我们的网站上，还有本期的小测验和练习题，网址是 bbclearningenglish.com。现在该说再见了。

Becca：Bye!

Becca：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（哪些邮件让人觉得粗鲁，战斗反应和逃跑反应在邮件里分别是什么样，怎么避免），6 个表达都知道意思，Phil 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. His angry question really put me on the ______.（让我产生戒备）
  2. It's ______ to ignore a colleague's email for a week.（无礼的）
  3. A good manager never tries to ______ the team in front of customers.（贬低）
  4. After three meetings and fifty emails, I felt completely ______.（疲惫焦躁的）
  5. He passed the report to me just to get it off his ______.（把事情甩出去）
  6. The ______ is Friday, so please send me your part by Thursday.（截止日期）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，Elon Musk，Phil 猜的是 JD Vance，答错了。两个听众的例子：开头只写名字、不打招呼的邮件；精心写的邮件只收到一个表情符号的回复。填空：1. defensive 2. uncivil 3. belittle 4. frazzled 5. plate 6. deadline

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 1 和 G 类写信做准备）：Do you prefer to communicate with colleagues by email or face to face? 用英语说两三句：I usually prefer ... because ... / Emails are useful when ..., but ...。另外想一想：给经理写信时，开头用 Dear Mr Smith 还是只写 Smith，哪个更礼貌？
